item.title: Tomonoura: A Timeless Inland Sea Port Town — Guide
item.description: Tomonoura, on a headland south of Fukuyama, is one of the best-preserved old harbour towns on the Seto Inland Sea, so little changed that walking its lanes feels like stepping into the Edo period. Ships once waited here for the tide to turn, and the town grew wealthy on that trade, leaving a rare survival: the original stone-built harbour with its curved jetty, a squat stone lighthouse, warehouses and temples, and streets of wooden merchant houses.

item.title: Narai-juku: A Beautifully Preserved Edo-Era Post Town — Guide
item.description: Narai-juku is one of the best-preserved post towns (shukuba) on the old Nakasendo, the Edo-period highway that connected Tokyo and Kyoto through the mountains, and was historically one of the most prosperous stops thanks to its position before a difficult mountain pass. Today its roughly one-kilometre street of dark wooden merchant houses, traditional inns, craft shops and cafes is preserved largely intact, letting visitors walk through an atmospheric slice of Edo-era travel history far quieter than Japan’s more famous historic streets.
